Property management services in Bayonne

Tenant placement

We market your Bayonne rental across top listing platforms. Every applicant goes through income verification on the tenant’s share of the rent, a credit and rental history review, and background screening as New Jersey law allows.

Rent collection

Automated online collection with direct owner disbursements. Late fees handled per NJ law. Real-time visibility in your owner portal.

Maintenance coordination

24/7 tenant maintenance requests. Vendor network covering Hudson County. Owners approve repairs above their stated threshold.

Financial reporting

Monthly owner statements and 24/7 portal access.

NJ compliance

PPM stays current on Bayonne and statewide NJ landlord-tenant law — security deposits, habitability, lease requirements, and eviction procedures.

The Bayonne rental market

Bayonne sits on a peninsula between Jersey City and Staten Island, with the Hudson-Bergen Light Rail and quick access to the Holland Tunnel and the Turnpike. It is one of Hudson County's more attainable rental markets — heavy on two- and three-family homes and converted rowhouses — and draws commuters priced out of Hoboken and Downtown Jersey City. Waterfront redevelopment around Cape Liberty keeps adding newer inventory.

The bread-and-butter here is small multi-family: duplexes, triplexes, and modest walk-ups. Tenant placement, fast turnovers, and upkeep of older stock are where day-to-day management matters most. Bayonne is also a rent-control municipality, so registering covered units and staying current on the city’s ordinance is part of managing here.

Why Bayonne owners work with PPM

We lease to Bayonne's commuter renter pool with full screening, coordinate maintenance across a Hudson County vendor network, and keep every property compliant with NJ landlord-tenant law — one flat fee and real-time owner-portal visibility, whether you own a single duplex or a small portfolio.

Bayonne has rent control.

Bayonne’s rent control ordinance now covers only units in buildings of five or more units whose tenant has been in place since June 30, 2011. For those units, an increase must be approved by the Rent Control Office, follows the CPI and is capped at 5.5%, and the tenant must be registered each year. We keep every increase, notice, and registration compliant — and track the current cap and exemptions for you.
